citation_network._purpose: Citation-network / domain-concentration analysis of df_citations.parquet (22,903 rows). $0 CPU. Non-canonical staging (NOT merged into canonical_numbers.json).
citation_network._data: data/analysis/df_citations.parquet (main, Bing backend) + df_citations_protocol_a.parquet (has backend col). Non-placeholder = category in {real_url,academic,suspicious}. Quality joins use mean over 3 judges {gpt52,opus,sonnet}.

concentration_findings.echo_chamber_verdict: NO severe echo chamber at architecture level: domain HHI is uniformly LOW (0.007-0.044) and Gini 0.25-0.48 across all 12 arms. Most concentrated arm is P2 (top-1 domain arxiv.org = 19.8% of cites, HHI 0.0435) - a mild arxiv over-reliance; every other arm's top domain is <11%.
concentration_findings.most_diverse: p3 (unique_ratio 0.727) and p11 (0.731) spread cites over the most distinct domains; p5 is least diverse (unique_ratio 0.406).
concentration_findings.placeholder_flag: Several 'strong' pipelines pad citations with fabricated/placeholder URLs: p4 61.6%, p3 59.1%, p8 56.8%, p5 50.8%, p10 37.0% of their citations are placeholders (vs p0/p6/p7/p1 <1%). Concentration/diversity above is computed on the NON-placeholder remainder.

academic_vs_web.finding: Web sources dominate every arm (54-79% web). Academic share is highest for the local 7B P9 (0.46) and single-round P8 (0.37); lowest for verbose web-scrapers P11 (0.21) and P5 (0.22). No arm is majority-academic.

diversity_vs_quality.level: per (pattern,query_id) cell; quality = mean over 3 judges
diversity_vs_quality.finding: Raw domain COUNT tracks quality only because it proxies citation volume: after controlling for n_cites, n_unique_domains->overall collapses to ~0 (partial -0.017, ns). But EVENNESS of sourcing (Shannon entropy) SURVIVES the volume control: shannon->citation_quality partial +0.444 (p=1e-46), ->overall +0.354, ->factual +0.267. Genuine source diversity predicts quality independent of citation count; citing more academic sources does NOT raise citation_quality (raw pearson +0.001, ns).

backend_confound.finding: DECISIVE search-backend confound (protocol-A subset): the Tavily backend produces an EXTREME echo chamber - 76.2% of ALL citations to arxiv.org, HHI 0.596 (near-monopoly), 89.5% academic - vs Bing 13.1% arxiv, HHI 0.025, 35.6% academic. Source concentration is driven far more by the retrieval backend than by the orchestration architecture; any cross-architecture diversity claim must hold backend fixed.

citation_network.verdict: No architecture is an echo chamber (HHI<=0.044); P2's mild arxiv over-reliance (~20%) is the ceiling. Source diversity DOES help quality, but only as EVENNESS (Shannon, partial +0.44 on citation_quality), not raw domain count (a citation-volume proxy) and not academic share. The dominant driver of source concentration is the SEARCH BACKEND (Tavily 76% arxiv / HHI 0.60), a confound that swamps architecture.

mvt_foraging._purpose: Charnov Marginal Value Theorem (MVT) over-foraging test: do iterative/reactive pipelines search past the point of diminishing marginal evidence yield, and does over-foraging buy any citation/quality gain? $0 CPU.
mvt_foraging._data_and_coverage: Within-run marginal-yield curves from checkpoints/<pattern>/<ts>/trace.json tool_calls (ordered by step_idx, n_results per retrieval verb). Arm-level effort/yield/score from canonical search_robustness + compute_ledger + per_dimension. COVERAGE CAVEAT: traces cover ~30/90 canonical qids for most pipelines (p0=43, p9=83); P11/P12 have NO usable traces. Raw n_results is verb-name-specific (NOT cross-architecture comparable) and does NOT dedup within run, so it OVERSTATES late-search value (any decline found is conservative). Per-call unique-URL dedup is not logged.

mvt_threshold_env_avg_yield.definition: Cross-source (environment) average marginal yield = grand mean n_results per 'search' call pooled across all 8 traced pipelines (n=4048 calls). MVT-optimal stop = when a pipeline's marginal new-doc yield falls to this environment average.

p1_iterative_rag.finding: STEEP diminishing returns: search 1 yields 8.3 docs, search 2 = 1.3, search 4 = 1.0 (8.3x collapse). ~93% of P1's search calls are issued AFTER marginal yield has already dropped below the environment average - a fixed-iteration loop that keeps foraging in an exhausted patch.

p6_reactive_interleaved.finding: Raw per-search yield does NOT decline (17.3 at step 1 -> 26.2 at step 13) because P6 targets a fresh subtopic each reactive step; raw n_results is not NEW-doc yield. MVT cannot be cleanly tested for P6 on raw counts (per-call dedup unlogged). P6 issues a FIXED 13 searches/run regardless of marginal value - no model-driven early stop.

p10_deep_researcher.finding: PATHOLOGICAL over-forager: all 17.4 search actions/run return 0 retrieved docs via the search verb (its docs arrive through tool_call/source_extract). 100% of its searches sit below the MVT stop, yet it keeps issuing up to 24. Extreme effort, near-zero search harvest.

arm_level_effort_vs_outcome.finding: DECISIVE consequence test (11 arms): searching MORE buys NOTHING. n_searches vs score pearson -0.336 (ns), vs citation_quality -0.178 (ns), vs factual -0.336 (ns), vs surviving citations -0.155 (ns), and vs docs actually retrieved +0.022 (ns). Every correlation is <=0 or null. The two heaviest foragers are the two worst outcomes-per-effort: P10 (24.4 searches -> score 0.336, LOWEST; 0.19 surviving citations/search) and P6 (13 searches -> 1.89 citations/search, same harvest efficiency as P0 which searches 4.6x less, at 18x P0's wall-clock).

mvt_optimal_stoppers.finding: The STRONG pipelines approximate the MVT stop: the top scorers forage little and quit early - P8 (1 search, 0.625, 34.8 citations/search), P4 (1 search, 0.640, 21.2/search), P7 (3 searches, 0.630), P1 (4 searches, 0.673). P0 reaches 0.488 in 2.8 searches, beating P10 (0.336) with 1/8th the foraging. Harvest efficiency (surviving citations per search) is INVERSELY related to search volume.

mvt_foraging.verdict: MVT holds as a diagnosis. (1) Where searches truly share a doc pool, marginal yield collapses fast (P1 8.3x over 4 searches; P5 widen->deepen 12.3x), and pipelines keep foraging past the environment-average stop (P1: 93% of searches). (2) The RL agent P10 is the extreme MVT violator: ~17 search actions/run, marginal new-unique-doc slope only +0.14 URLs per extra search (vs env avg 13.3), and it scores LOWEST. (3) Over-foraging correlates with ZERO quality/citation gain across 11 arms (all n_searches correlations <=0, ns). The strong architectures (P1/P4/P7/P8) implicitly obey MVT by stopping after 1-4 well-targeted searches. CAVEAT: raw-yield MVT cannot be tested per-call for P6 (fixed 13 searches, no dedup); trace coverage ~30/90 qids; P11/P12 untraced.
